function: MIMO beam-pair selection at the base station for a UAV receiver: a decision tree maps UAV coordinates to the best DFT-codebook beam pair (p. 7, p. 9).
system: Sionna ray tracing, 40 GHz; base station 8x8 UPA, UAV receiver 2x2 UPA; DFT codebooks of 64 and 4 beams; no RIS (p. 9).
method: Decision tree (scikit-learn, maximum depth 15), supervised classification of the beam-pair index (256 classes) from UAV coordinates, trained offline (p. 9, p. 10).
data_channel: Self-generated Sionna ray tracing of an OpenStreetMap Central Park scene; 1274 scenes (NLOS only) split 70/30 into training and validation; separate test trajectory (p. 8, p. 9, p. 10).
test_conditions: Trained and validated on random-waypoint flights (70/30 split); tested on a separately generated trajectory in the same Central Park scene, transmitter and carrier (p. 8, p. 10).
baselines: Random beam-pair choice and an oracle (best pair from the data set), both non-learned; no other learned beam-selection method is compared (p. 8).
metrics: Top-K beam accuracy; SAR mission time, rescued targets; PSNR of degraded images; CPU, RAM, GPU use; wall-clock time and real-time factor (p. 8, p. 10, p. 11, p. 12).
complexity: Co-simulation cost: CPU, RAM, GPU use per module (p. 11); wall-clock time and real-time factor for 60 s of simulation (p. 12); nothing for the decision tree.
openness: Code promised upon publication at github.com/lasseufpa/caviar (p. 2 footnote); no data released.
q1_support: p. 9: "UAV coordinates to Sionna, which executes RT" - channels come from the authors' own ray tracing of an OpenStreetMap scene; only the antenna pattern is TR38901 (Table V); no standardized channel model, public dataset or measured data.
q2_support: p. 10: "we generated a separate test trajectory" - same Central Park scene, transmitter, carrier and arrays as in training; no new scenario, configuration or site.
q3_support: p. 8: "ML-based beam selection: random and oracle" - both baselines are non-learned; no earlier learned beam-selection method or standard learner is compared.
q4_support: p. 12: "Total wall-clock time for executing 60 seconds of simulation" - measured runtime of the co-simulation (Fig. 12), with CPU, RAM and GPU use in Fig. 11 (p. 11); nothing for the decision tree itself.
q5_support: p. 2: "The project code will be made available upon publication" - link github.com/lasseufpa/caviar is given, but the release is promised, not made, in this version; no data released.
notes: Preprint (arXiv v1) of a co-simulation platform paper. Borderline inclusion: the platform is the contribution and the learned part is a demonstration decision tree for beam selection (p. 6, p. 7), kept because it is trained, evaluated (Table VI) and drives the mission results. Area 6 because the beams serve a UAV (aerial link); area 3 if the UAV is treated only as a user of a terrestrial base station. q4 counts the cost of the proposed platform, not of the tree; the reviewer should confirm. q5: check the published version or the repository for the actual release.
